title: Reusable Web Component (custom element)
when: The user wants a reusable widget as its own HTML tag that works on any page without a framework.
prompt:
Goal: A custom element with a clear tag, attributes and events, encapsulated styles and proper cleanup.
Steps:
1. Name it with a hyphen (rating-stars) and register once: if (!customElements.get(name)) customElements.define(name, Klass).
2. Constructor: only super() and attachShadow({ mode: "open" }); build content in connectedCallback, when attributes are ready.
3. List static observedAttributes and update in attributeChangedCallback; mirror key attributes as properties.
4. Clone a <template> with its own <style> into the shadow root; theme through custom properties and ::part; <slot> for user content.
5. Emit changes with new CustomEvent("change", { detail, bubbles: true, composed: true }); remove document listeners and timers in disconnectedCallback.
Quality bar:
- Keyboard usable, with accessible names inside the shadow root.
- Works from markup alone: tag plus attributes.
- Upgrades cleanly when the script loads late.
Pitfalls:
- Reading attributes or children in the constructor.
- Writing attribute values into innerHTML, which allows injection; use textContent.
- Forgetting composed: true, so events never leave the shadow root.
Verify:
- [ ] The tag has a hyphen and define is guarded.
- [ ] observedAttributes lists every reactive attribute.
- [ ] disconnectedCallback cleans up.
- [ ] A demo page uses the tag with real content.
Output: components/<name>.js defining the element and a demo index.html importing it as a module.

examples.input: make a <star-rating> tag I can reuse
examples.output: star-rating element with value and max attributes, radio buttons in shadow DOM, change event with detail.value
